name: Floor & Wall Tiling, Marble & Stone, Hard Flooring

activities: confirm waterproofing flood-tested and protected (wet areas)
confirm screed cured to moisture spec
confirm falls to drains and level datum
sequence.note: Tiling cannot start until waterproofing is signed and screed moisture is within spec; covering wet/untested substrate is the top cause of tile failure.

activities: establish datum lines and tile grid from architect's setting-out
dry-lay to balance cuts and match features
mark expansion/movement joint locations
shade/vein matching for stone slabs
sequence.note: Setting-out is agreed against door thresholds, drains and feature centrelines before any adhesive.

activities: slurry/scratch coat or mortar bed for natural stone
backing preparation and sealing of porous stone rear (anti-staining)
confirm substrate flatness for large-format/stone
sequence.note: Marble/stone needs a fully prepared, flat, non-staining substrate; laying stone on an unready bed causes lippage and picture-framing stains.

activities: notch-trowel adhesive / full-buttering for large format
lay to falls in wet areas
cut to gullies, penetrations, thresholds
maintain movement joints
sequence.note: Fall to gully is maintained through the tile plane; movement joints are never bridged with rigid grout.

activities: wall tiling over cementitious background
stone cladding with mechanical anchors where required
coordinate with sanitary fixings and niches
grout (epoxy in wet/heavy-duty)
seal natural stone and grout lines
install movement/silicone joints at perimeters and changes of plane
sequence.note: Perimeter and internal corners get flexible sealant, not grout, to absorb movement.

activities: board/protect finished floor
acid-free clean of stone
hand over protected surface
sequence.note: Finished stone/tile is protected immediately; following trades work over protection.

typical_relationships.reason: tiling over untested tanking hides leaks and forces tile demolition to repair the membrane
adhesives over green screed debond; moisture migrates and stains natural stone
stone laid on an unready or porous substrate suffers lippage, hollowness and rear-face staining
tiles laid without agreed setting-out create bad cuts at thresholds and break the fall to gully
WCs, basins, mixers and accessories mount onto or through finished tiling; fixing before tiling blocks the tile plane

typical_relationships.after: final floor tiling in same room
typical_relationships.reason: finished floors are damaged by overhead work; where possible ceilings/paint precede or floors are protected

interfaces.requirement: membrane cured, flood-tested (signed) and protected before wet-area tiling; adhesive compatible with membrane
screed cured to moisture spec and laid to falls; wet-wall background cementitious
floor gullies, drains and penetration levels fixed so tile falls run to them and cuts land cleanly
tiling complete and set-out to fixture centrelines before sanitaryware, accessories and mixers are mounted through/onto tile
finished floor levels coordinated with door undercuts, thresholds and skirting/joinery datums

commissioning_dependencies: fall-to-gully verified on finished tile before fixtures
stone sealing complete before wet commissioning
testing_requirements: grout/joint continuity and sealed movement joints
typical_exceptions: raised-access floor or vinyl/resin flooring replaces bedded tile in offices/labs - different substrate rules
stone rainscreen/cladding on walls is a facade-adjacent mechanically-fixed package
pre-cured large-format thin porcelain needs specialist backing and handling
external frost-rated paving ties to landscape/drainage rather than internal wet zones
evidence: Tiling/stone constructability is dominated by two upstream gates - cured screed and signed waterproofing - and hands off to sanitary/second-fix downstream. Setting-out, fall-to-gully, movement joints and stone substrate preparation are trade universals. Generalized across residential and commercial fit-out; no project data embedded.
